# GEMS SDK Java — AI Context File

This file is intended for AI assistants (Claude, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini, etc.) consuming this repository.
It follows the llmstxt.org convention and is kept up-to-date with the public API surface.

---

## What is this

GEMS SDK (`br.com.gems:gems-sdk`) is a multi-module Maven library of shared, reusable resources consumed by GEMS microservices.
It is published as JARs to GitHub Packages — it is NOT a runnable application.

- **Current version:** 3.0.0
- **Java:** 21
- **Spring Boot parent:** 4.1.0
- **GroupId:** `br.com.gems`
- **GitHub Packages URL:** `https://maven.pkg.github.com/Gabriel-mDias/Java-GEMS-SDK`
- **Architecture:** Spring Boot starter-style auto-configuration — consumers add the dependency and optionally set a property; no `@Import` or `@ComponentScan` needed. Three modules ship no auto-configuration on purpose (`gems-mapstruct`, `gems-keycloak-admin`, `gems-security-authorization`) — see their sections.

### What 3.0.0 adds and changes

**Four new modules**, all additive: `gems-mapstruct`, `gems-auditing`, `gems-keycloak-admin`, `gems-security-authorization`. Nothing is deprecated anywhere in the SDK, and `gems-model-mapper` remains first-class and supported.

In **fifteen of the sixteen modules** no existing public API changed signature or was removed. The exception is `gems-jpa-multi-tenant`, whose rewrite is source-incompatible — see below. Verified against the `2.0.1` baseline before release.

**One module changes observable behaviour and breaks its public API**: `gems-jpa-multi-tenant`. That module alone is why this is a **MAJOR** release — everywhere else the release is strictly additive. It had zero declared consumers in the 2.x range at release time (re-verified immediately before publishing), but the version states the contract, not the consumer count. The changes:

1. Fail-closed by default — persisting with no tenant in context raises `TenantContextMissingException` instead of falling back to a default schema.
2. `TenantScope` is the supported way to enter/leave a tenant; it closes on exception and restores the previous scope rather than clearing the context.
3. One schema prefix, read in one place (`TenantSchemaNaming`), default now **`tenant_`** (was two conflicting defaults, `instituicao_` and `client_tenant_`, read in three places).
4. Migrations run at **provisioning**; the persistence path only checks and refuses with `TenantSchemaNotReadyException`.
5. Global scope must be explicit and requires `gems.tenant.global-schema` — there is no default.

Its **public API is also source-incompatible**, which is why "additive" does not describe this module: `JpaTenantContext` is now `final` with a private constructor (was an extensible/instantiable class); its `public static final String DEFAULT_TENANT = "public"` was **removed** (fail-closed leaves no default to name); and `MultiTenantLiquibaseConfig` moved from `MultiTenantLiquibaseConfig(DataSource)` plus `@Value` fields to a four-argument constructor and is no longer a `@Component` — it is wired by configuration. Code written against `2.0.x` of this module does not compile against `3.0.0`.

`gems-exception` gained a uniform error envelope and handlers for 400 (validation), 403 (`AccessDeniedException`) and 502 (external service), additively.

---

## Golden Rules

### DO

- Always use `gems-bom` to manage versions — declare one version in `<dependencyManagement>` and omit `<version>` on individual modules.
- Activate opt-in modules via `application.yml` flags (see Property Reference below).
- Prefer `TenantScope.forTenant(alias)` / `TenantScope.global()` (try-with-resources) over `JpaTenantContext.setCurrentTenant` / `clear`. It closes on exception and restores the previous scope, so nesting works.
- If you do use `JpaTenantContext` directly, always clear it in a `finally` block — failure causes tenant state to leak across pooled threads.
- Be explicit about data that belongs to no organization: open `TenantScope.global()`. Since 3.0.0 there is no silent fallback schema.
- Use `@Mapper(config = GemsMappingConfig.class)` for new mappers (`gems-mapstruct`). `gems-model-mapper` is still supported — don't migrate working code just for this.
- Mark audited entities with `@Auditable`, and sensitive fields with `@SensitiveField` (records that the field changed, not its values).
- Declare authorization intent on every endpoint: `@PublicEndpoint`, `@GlobalEndpoint` or `@TenantEndpoint`.
- Combine `@ValidCpf` / `@ValidCnpj` / `@ValidEmail` with `@NotNull` when the field is mandatory — the constraints treat `null` as valid by design.
- Use `ApiResponseDTO.ok(data)` or `ApiResponseDTO.ok(data, message)` to wrap success responses in REST controllers.
- Use `BusinessException` for business rule violations (HTTP 400) and `SecurityException` for auth failures (HTTP 401).
- Use `ModelMapperUtils.mapStrict()` when you need STRICT strategy mapping to avoid ambiguity errors.
- Use `PageResponseDTO.from(page)` to convert a Spring `Page<T>` to a serializable DTO.
- Inject Spring beans (`S3Service`, `TenantSchemaService`, etc.) via constructor injection (`@RequiredArgsConstructor`) — never instantiate them directly.
- To bump the SDK version: `mvn versions:set -DnewVersion=<NEW_VERSION> -DgenerateBackupPoms=false` from the repo root.

### DON'T

- Never edit `<version>` in any `pom.xml` manually — it breaks the inheritance chain and the CI build.
- Never add `@Import` or `@ComponentScan` for SDK classes — they register themselves via Spring Boot auto-configuration.
- Never instantiate `S3Service`, `GlobalExceptionHandler`, or other SDK beans directly — inject them.
- Never forget to set `aws.s3.enabled=true` and `aws.s3.bucket-name` when adding `gems-aws`.
- Never call `JpaTenantContext.setCurrentTenant()` without a matching `JpaTenantContext.clear()` in a `finally` block.
- Never add `gems-jpa-multi-tenant` without also enabling `gems-jpa` (`gems.jpa.enabled=true`).
- Never hardcode dependency versions in module poms — all third-party versions are centralized in the root `pom.xml` `<properties>`.
- Never declare your own `@Value("${gems.tenant.schema-prefix}")`. `TenantSchemaNaming` is the single reader; a second one reintroduces the defect where migrations ran against one schema while traffic read from another, with no error anywhere.
- Never lower `unmappedTargetPolicy` from `ERROR` to `WARN` in `gems-mapstruct`. Every compile failure it produces is a target field that would otherwise arrive null in silence.
- Never inject an audit service into a domain service — there isn't one. `TransactionalAuditWriter` is package-private on purpose; a Hibernate `Integrator` installs the listener.
- Never give `KeycloakAdminProperties` a default value or commit a client secret. Missing `baseUrl`, `realm`, `clientId` or `clientSecret` is rejected at construction so the environment fails at startup, not in production.
- Never authorize by generic role (`GESTOR`). Authorization is by concrete action (`AREA_VERBO`), derived from the consumer's enum; `AuthorizationCatalog` rejects anything else.
- Never hand-maintain the frontend action list — generate it with `FrontendActionCatalogGenerator`.

---

## Module Reference Table

| artifactId | Purpose | Activation flag | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gems-bom` | Bill of Materials — version alignment only | N/A | N/A |
| `gems-utils` | Pure utility classes (date, email, document, UUID, object) | None (auto-loaded) | always on |
| `gems-model-mapper` | Auto-configured `ModelMapper` bean — supported, not deprecated | `@ConditionalOnMissingBean` | always on |
| `gems-mapstruct` | `GemsMappingConfig` — shared MapStruct `@MapperConfig`, **recommended for new code** | None (no auto-config) | N/A |
| `gems-exception` | Global `@RestControllerAdvice` exception handler — uniform envelope, 400/403/502 | None (auto-loaded) | always on |
| `gems-jpa` | Base JPA repository abstractions | `gems.jpa.enabled=true` | false |
| `gems-jpa-multi-tenant` | Schema-per-tenant multi-tenancy (requires gems-jpa) — **fail-closed since 3.0.0** | `gems.tenant.enabled=true` | false |
| `gems-auditing` | Hibernate-level audit trail, opt-in per entity via `@Auditable` | `gems.auditing.enabled=true` (+ `gems.auditing.schema`) | false |
| `gems-keycloak-admin` | `KeycloakAdminGateway` — identity-provider admin operations; failures become 502 | None (no auto-config) | N/A |
| `gems-security-authorization` | Authorization by concrete action, derived from the consumer's enum | None (no auto-config) | N/A |
| `gems-aws` | S3 client + service beans (no web) | `aws.s3.enabled=true` | false |
| `gems-aws-web` | Optional S3 REST endpoints | `aws.s3.enabled=true` (same flag) | false |
| `gems-rest-common` | `ApiResponseDTO`, `PageResponseDTO`, `CorrelationIdFilter` | `gems.rest.correlation-id.enabled=true` | true |
| `gems-validation` | `@ValidCpf`, `@ValidCnpj`, `@ValidEmail` Bean Validation constraints | None (auto-discovered via `@Constraint`) | always on |
| `gems-openapi` | Springdoc OpenAPI auto-configuration | `gems.openapi.enabled=true` | true |
| `gems-observability` | Registers `ObservedAspect` to enable `@Observed` | `gems.observability.enabled=true` | true |

## Maven Coordinates & BOM Usage

### Step 1 — Add the repository

```xml
<repositories>
    <repository>
        <id>github</id>
        <name>GitHub Packages</name>
        <url>https://maven.pkg.github.com/Gabriel-mDias/Java-GEMS-SDK</url>
    </repository>
</repositories>
```

Authentication in `~/.m2/settings.xml`:
```xml
<servers>
    <server>
        <id>github</id>
        <username>YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME</username>
        <password>YOUR_GITHUB_TOKEN</password>
    </server>
</servers>
```

### Step 2 — Import the BOM

```xml
<dependencyManagement>
    <dependencies>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>br.com.gems</groupId>
            <artifactId>gems-bom</artifactId>
            <version>3.0.0</version>
            <type>pom</type>
            <scope>import</scope>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>
</dependencyManagement>
```

### Step 3 — Declare modules (no version needed)

```xml
<dependencies>
    <dependency>
        <groupId>br.com.gems</groupId>
        <artifactId>gems-utils</artifactId>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
        <groupId>br.com.gems</groupId>
        <artifactId>gems-exception</artifactId>
    </dependency>
    <!-- add more modules as needed -->
</dependencies>
```

## Per-Module API

---

### gems-utils

**Package:** `br.com.gems.utils`
**No Spring dependencies — pure Java.**

#### DateUtil

```java
DateUtil.isValidBirthDate(LocalDate date)     // true if date is in the past
DateUtil.isValidBirthDate(LocalDateTime date) // overload for LocalDateTime
```

#### DocumentoUtil

```java
DocumentoUtil.isDocumentoValid(String doc, TipoNumeroDocumentoEnum tipo) // generic
DocumentoUtil.isCpfValid(String cpf)    // accepts masked (000.000.000-00) or unmasked
DocumentoUtil.isCnpjValid(String cnpj)  // accepts masked or unmasked
```

**Enum:** `TipoNumeroDocumentoEnum` — values: `CPF`, `CNPJ`

#### EmailUtil

```java
EmailUtil.isValid(String email) // regex-based format check
```

#### ObjectUtil

```java
ObjectUtil.isNullOrEmpty(Object obj)          // handles String, Collection, null
ObjectUtil.isNotNullAndNotEmpty(Object obj)   // inverse
```

#### UUIDUtil

```java
UUIDUtil.fromStringOrNull(String id) // returns UUID or null (never throws)
```

**Other Enum:** `TipoSanguineoEnum` — blood type constants (A+, A-, B+, B-, O+, O-, AB+, AB-)

---

### gems-model-mapper

**Package:** `br.com.gems.mapper`
**Auto-configuration:** `GemsModelMapperAutoConfiguration` (registered automatically)

Creates a single `ModelMapper` bean configured with:
- `AmbiguityIgnored = true`
- Lazy field detection to skip uninitialized Hibernate proxies

```java
// Static utility — no injection needed
ModelMapperUtils.mapStrict(Object source, Class<D> destinationType) // returns D
ModelMapperUtils.mapStrict(Object source, Object destination)       // in-place mapping
```

Consumers can override the `ModelMapper` bean by declaring their own `@Bean ModelMapper` — the SDK's is `@ConditionalOnMissingBean`.

**Status: first-class and supported.** MapStruct is *recommended* for new code, not mandatory; this module is not deprecated and is not going away.

---

### gems-mapstruct

**Package:** `br.com.gems.mapstruct`
**Auto-configuration:** none — the module is a shared mapping configuration, not a bean
**Activation:** none

```java
@MapperConfig(componentModel = "spring", unmappedTargetPolicy = ReportingPolicy.ERROR)
public interface GemsMappingConfig {}
```

Usage — every consumer mapper references it:

```java
@Mapper(config = GemsMappingConfig.class)
public interface OrganizacaoMapper {
    OrganizacaoResponse toResponse(Organizacao source);
}
```

Package convention: `<domain>/mapper/XxxMapper`. `componentModel = "spring"` means the generated mapper is an injectable bean.

**`unmappedTargetPolicy = ERROR` is not to be relaxed.** A target field with no source **fails compilation**, naming the field. Adopting this in an existing project will fail builds — each failure is a field that arrives null in silence today. Lowering it to `WARN` removes the module's reason to exist; treat the fields one by one instead.

**Annotation processing gotcha:** the module puts `mapstruct-processor` on the compile classpath so a consumer that declares no `annotationProcessorPaths` gets generation by discovery. A consumer that *does* declare `annotationProcessorPaths` must add `lombok-mapstruct-binding` (after Lombok) and `mapstruct-processor` (last) there. Omitting it **does not break compilation** — it silently stops generating the mapper.

---

### gems-exception

**Package:** `br.com.gems.exception`
**Auto-configuration:** `GemsExceptionAutoConfiguration` (registered automatically)

#### Exception classes

```java
// Business rule violation → HTTP 400
new BusinessException(ErrorTypeEnum type, String message)
new BusinessException(String message)              // defaults to ErrorTypeEnum.FALHA
new BusinessException(List<String> messages)       // multi-error

// Authentication failure → HTTP 401
new SecurityException(String message)

// External service unavailable → HTTP 502   (3.0.0)
new ExternalServiceException(String servico, String message)
new ExternalServiceException(String servico, String message, Throwable causa)
```

#### ErrorTypeEnum

```java
ErrorTypeEnum.ERRO_NAO_ESPERADO  // unexpected system error (500)
ErrorTypeEnum.FALHA              // business rule failure (400)
ErrorTypeEnum.ALERTA             // business rule warning (400)
ErrorTypeEnum.VALIDACAO          // validation failure (400)        (3.0.0)
ErrorTypeEnum.ACESSO_NEGADO      // authorization denied (403)      (3.0.0)
ErrorTypeEnum.SERVICO_INDISPONIVEL // external service down (502)   (3.0.0)
```

#### ExceptionResponseDTO (response body — the uniform envelope)

```json
{
  "occurrenceTime": "2026-06-21T10:00:00",
  "errorType": "FALHA",
  "message": "CPF já cadastrado",
  "path": "/api/usuarios",
  "method": "POST",
  "codigo": "CPF_DUPLICADO",
  "detalhes": ["campo cpf: já existe"]
}
```

`codigo` and `detalhes` were added in 3.0.0 — additively; existing fields are unchanged.

#### Handlers (registered automatically)

| Exception | HTTP Status |
|---|---|
| `BusinessException` | 400 |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | 400 |
| `MethodArgumentNotValidException` | 400 (3.0.0) |
| `SecurityException` | 401 |
| `BadCredentialsException`, `AuthorizationDeniedException` | 401 (`SecurityExceptionHandler`) |
| `AccessDeniedException` | **403** (3.0.0 — `AuthorizationExceptionHandler`) |
| `ExternalServiceException` | **502** (3.0.0) |
| `Exception` (catch-all) | 500 |

403, not 401, for `AccessDeniedException`: whoever reached the handler is authenticated; what is missing is authorization.

---

### gems-jpa

**Package:** `br.com.gems.jpa`
**Auto-configuration:** `JpaConfig`
**Activation:** `gems.jpa.enabled=true`
**Property:** `gems.jpa.base-packages` (default: `br.com.gems`)

#### BaseCustomJpaRepository<T> — interface to extend

```java
// COUNT queries
Long executeCountHql(StringBuilder hql)
Long executeCountHql(StringBuilder hql, Map<String, Object> params)

// SELECT queries
<R> List<R> executeHql(StringBuilder hql, Class<R> clazz)
<R> List<R> executeHql(StringBuilder hql, Map<String, Object> params, Class<R> clazz)
<R> Page<R>  executeHql(StringBuilder hql, Pageable pageable, Class<R> clazz)
<R> Page<R>  executeHql(StringBuilder hql, Map<String, Object> params, Pageable pageable, Class<R> clazz)

// Native SQL
<R> List<R> executeNativeQuery(StringBuilder sql, Class<R> clazz)
<R> List<R> executeNativeQuery(StringBuilder sql, Map<String, Object> params, Class<R> clazz)
```

```yaml
# application.yml
gems:
  jpa:
    enabled: true
    base-packages: br.com.seuprojeto
```

#### Canonical Repository Pattern

The correct pattern for GEMS repositories is a **single interface** that:
1. Extends both `JpaRepository<Entity, ID>` and `BaseCustomJpaRepository<Entity>`
2. Declares Spring Data derived-query methods (`findBy*`, `existsBy*`, etc.)
3. Contains `default` methods for complex searches that delegate to `private` HQL builder methods
4. Uses `ObjectUtil.isNotNullAndNotEmpty()` to guard dynamic filter parameters

```java
@Repository
public interface PedidoRepository extends JpaRepository<Pedido, UUID>, BaseCustomJpaRepository<Pedido> {

    // Spring Data derived queries — declared normally
    Optional<Pedido> findByClienteIdAndStatus(UUID clienteId, StatusPedidoEnum status);
    boolean existsByClienteIdAndDataCancelamentoIsNull(UUID clienteId);

    // Public search entry point — builds the Page from count + query
    default Page<PedidoResponseDTO> search(PedidoFilterParams filterParams, Pageable pageable) {
        return new PageImpl<>(
            searchQuery(filterParams, pageable),
            pageable,
            countQuery(filterParams)
        );
    }

    // Private count query — always mirrors the WHERE clause of searchQuery
    private Long countQuery(PedidoFilterParams filterParams) {
        var hql = new StringBuilder();
        var params = new HashMap<String, Object>();

        hql.append(" SELECT count(p.id) ");
        hql.append(" FROM Pedido p ");
        hql.append(" JOIN p.cliente c ");

        appendFilters(filterParams, hql, params);

        return this.executeCountHql(hql, params);
    }

    // Private data query — uses HQL constructor expression to map directly to DTO
    private List<PedidoResponseDTO> searchQuery(PedidoFilterParams filterParams, Pageable pageable) {
        var hql = new StringBuilder();
        var params = new HashMap<String, Object>();

        hql.append(" SELECT new br.com.seuprojeto.dto.PedidoResponseDTO( ");
        hql.append("   p.id, ");
        hql.append("   c.id, ");
        hql.append("   c.nome, ");
        hql.append("   p.status ) ");
        hql.append(" FROM Pedido p ");
        hql.append(" JOIN p.cliente c ");

        appendFilters(filterParams, hql, params);

        return this.executeHql(hql, params, pageable, PedidoResponseDTO.class);
    }

    // Private filter builder — shared by count and data queries
    private void appendFilters(PedidoFilterParams filterParams, StringBuilder hql, HashMap<String, Object> params) {
        hql.append(" WHERE 1=1 ");

        if (ObjectUtil.isNotNullAndNotEmpty(filterParams.getClienteNome())) {
            hql.append(" AND LOWER(c.nome) LIKE :clienteNome ");
            params.put("clienteNome", "%" + filterParams.getClienteNome().toLowerCase() + "%");
        }

        if (ObjectUtil.isNotNullAndNotEmpty(filterParams.getStatus())) {
            hql.append(" AND p.status = :status ");
            params.put("status", filterParams.getStatus());
        }
    }
}
```

**Key rules for this pattern:**
- `countQuery` and `searchQuery` must share the exact same `appendFilters` call — never diverge their WHERE clauses.
- Always use `WHERE 1=1` so `AND` conditions can be appended unconditionally.
- Use HQL constructor expressions (`SELECT new br.com.pacote.DTO(...)`) to map query results directly to DTOs without an extra mapping step.
- Use `LOWER(field) LIKE :param` with `toLowerCase()` on the value for case-insensitive text searches.
- Guard every dynamic filter with `ObjectUtil.isNotNullAndNotEmpty()` — never append a filter for a null/empty value.

#### Service layer usage

The service delegates to the repository `search` method and uses `ObjectUtil` for null guards before repository calls:

```java
@Service
@RequiredArgsConstructor
public class PedidoService {

    private final ModelMapper mapper;
    private final PedidoRepository repository;

    public Page<PedidoResponseDTO> search(PedidoFilterParams filterParams, Pageable pageable) {
        return repository.search(filterParams, pageable);
    }

    public PedidoDTO findById(UUID id) {
        if (ObjectUtil.isNullOrEmpty(id)) {
            throw new BusinessException("O id do pedido não foi informado!");
        }
        Pedido entity = repository.findById(id)
            .orElseThrow(() -> new BusinessException("Pedido não encontrado!"));
        return mapper.map(entity, PedidoDTO.class);
    }
}
```

---

### gems-jpa-multi-tenant

**Package:** `br.com.gems.tenant` (config in `br.com.gems.tenant.config`)
**Auto-configuration:** `MultiTenantJpaConfig` — every bean is `@ConditionalOnMissingBean`, so the consumer can replace any of them
**Activation:** `gems.tenant.enabled=true` (also requires `gems.jpa.enabled=true`)

> **BEHAVIOUR CHANGED IN 3.0.0.** See "What 3.0.0 adds and changes" at the top of this file before upgrading a project that used 2.0.x.

#### TenantScope — the supported way to enter and leave a tenant

```java
TenantScope.forTenant(String alias)              // AutoCloseable; alias cannot be "__global__"
TenantScope.global()                             // declared global scope
TenantScope.runInTenant(String alias, Runnable)
TenantScope.runInGlobal(Runnable)
TenantScope.callInTenant(String alias, Supplier<T>) // returns T
TenantScope.callInGlobal(Supplier<T>)               // returns T
scope.close()                                    // restores the PREVIOUS scope, not "no scope"
```

```java
try (TenantScope scope = TenantScope.forTenant("acme")) {
    repository.save(enrolment);
}

try (TenantScope scope = TenantScope.global()) {   // data that belongs to no organization
    repository.save(systemSetting);
}
```

Two guarantees: it closes even if the body throws, and closing **restores the previous scope** — without that, a global scope opened inside a tenant operation would leave the outer operation with no context on return.

#### JpaTenantContext — ThreadLocal context holder (lower-level)

```java
JpaTenantContext.GLOBAL_TENANT_IDENTIFIER        // "__global__"
JpaTenantContext.setCurrentTenant(String alias)  // rejects "__global__" — use TenantScope.global()
JpaTenantContext.getCurrentTenant()              // alias, or GLOBAL_TENANT_IDENTIFIER in global scope
                                                 // THROWS TenantContextMissingException with no scope
JpaTenantContext.current()                       // Optional<Snapshot>, does not throw
JpaTenantContext.clear()                         // MUST be called in finally block
record Snapshot(String alias, boolean global)    // global XOR alias — never both, never neither
```

`getCurrentTenant()` no longer falls back to a default schema. Absence of context is an error (MT-1); global is a scope somebody wrote.

#### Exceptions

```java
TenantContextMissingException   // no scope installed at persistence time
TenantSchemaNotReadyException   // schema exists in config but was not migrated at provisioning
TenantAliasConflictException    // alias resolution found a conflict
TenantMigrationException        // migration failed at provisioning
```

#### TenantSchemaNaming — the single source of the schema name

```java
TenantSchemaNaming.DEFAULT_SCHEMA_PREFIX          // "tenant_"
```

Reads `gems.tenant.schema-prefix` and `gems.tenant.global-schema`, and is the **only** place that does. Do not declare your own `@Value` for either. Asking for global scope without `gems.tenant.global-schema` fails instead of picking a schema by omission.

#### TenantSchemaService — tenant provisioning (this is where migrations run)

```java
// Injected as Spring bean
tenantSchemaService.createSchemaAndRunLiquibase(String acronym)
// Creates schema (e.g. "tenant_sigla") and runs Liquibase migrations
```

`TenantMigrationCoordinator` applies migrations at provisioning. The persistence path only **verifies** and refuses with `TenantSchemaNotReadyException` — running DDL in a request path would charge the first request of each organization for the migration and race between concurrent requests.

#### TenantIdentifierValidator — SQL injection guard (internal)

Called automatically before composing schema SQL. Tenant identifiers must be alphanumeric + underscore only.

#### Configuration

```yaml
gems:
  jpa:
    enabled: true
    base-packages: br.com.seuprojeto
  tenant:
    enabled: true
    schema-prefix: tenant_          # default since 3.0.0
    global-schema: administracao    # no default; TenantScope.global() fails without it
    client-query: SELECT DS_SIGLA_CLIENT FROM tenant_configuration.client
    liquibase:
      changelog: db/changelog/changelog-multi-schemas.xml
```

#### Canonical TenantFilter pattern (implement in consumer app)

Preserved, and correct only because of the `finally`. `TenantScope` gives the same guarantee without depending on discipline.

```java
@Slf4j
@Component
@RequiredArgsConstructor
public class TenantFilter extends OncePerRequestFilter {

    @Override
    protected void doFilterInternal(HttpServletRequest request,
                                    HttpServletResponse response,
                                    FilterChain filterChain) throws ServletException, IOException {
        Authentication auth = SecurityContextHolder.getContext().getAuthentication();
        if (auth instanceof JwtAuthenticationToken jwt) {
            String tenant = (String) jwt.getToken().getClaim("organization");
            if (tenant != null && !tenant.isBlank()) {
                JpaTenantContext.setCurrentTenant(tenant.toLowerCase());
            }
        }
        try {
            filterChain.doFilter(request, response);
        } finally {
            JpaTenantContext.clear(); // ALWAYS clear in finally
        }
    }
}
```

---

### gems-auditing

**Package:** `br.com.gems.auditing`
**Auto-configuration:** `AuditingAutoConfiguration`
**Activation:** `gems.auditing.enabled=true` **and** `gems.auditing.schema` (mandatory, no default)

Opt-in twice: the property enables the module, and each entity opts in.

```java
@Documented @Inherited @Target(TYPE) @Retention(RUNTIME)
public @interface Auditable {}      // opts the entity into the trail; inherited by subclasses

public @interface SensitiveField {} // records THAT the field changed, never its values
```

```java
public record AuditActor(String name, AuditActorType type) {}
public enum AuditActorType { USUARIO, TECNICO }
public enum AuditOperation { INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE }
public record AuditChange(String field, String oldValue, String newValue, boolean sensitive) {}
public class AuditWriteException extends RuntimeException {}
```

Extension points, both `@ConditionalOnMissingBean`:

```java
public interface AuditActorProvider { AuditActor currentActor(); }
// default: SystemAuditActorProvider — actor "SISTEMA". Replace it to record the authenticated user.

public interface AuditTrailDestination { String schemaFor(String entityName); }
// default: FixedSchemaAuditTrailDestination, reading gems.auditing.schema.
// Replace it to route the trail per organization.
```

**The domain never calls the writer.** `AuditHibernateIntegrator` installs `HibernateAuditListener`; `TransactionalAuditWriter` and the listener are package-private, and an architecture test asserts that nothing outside the module reaches the writer. Do not generate code that injects an audit service into a domain service — there is none to inject.

`gems.auditing.schema` has no built-in default on purpose: a default would make the SDK choose, by omission, between writing the trail next to the organization's data and writing it to a global schema — the one decision it must not take for the consumer.

```yaml
gems:
  auditing:
    enabled: true
    schema: auditoria
```

---

### gems-keycloak-admin

**Package:** `br.com.gems.keycloak.admin`
**Auto-configuration:** none — the consumer declares the bean
**Activation:** none

```java
public interface KeycloakAdminGateway {
    record User(String id, String name, String username, String email, boolean enabled) {}

    String ensureOrganization(String alias, String displayName);   // creates if absent
    void updateOrganization(String organizationId, String displayName);
    Optional<User> findUserByEmail(String email);
    User createUser(String name, String username, String email, String password);
    String ensureGroup(String organizationId, String groupName);   // group name is a PARAMETER
    void ensureRealmRoleOnGroup(String organizationId, String groupId, String role);
    void addOrganizationMember(String organizationId, String userId);
    void addGroupMember(String organizationId, String groupId, String userId);
    void removeGroupMember(String organizationId, String groupId, String userId);
}

public record KeycloakAdminProperties(String baseUrl, String realm, String clientId,
        String clientSecret, Duration connectTimeout, Duration readTimeout) {}

public final class KeycloakAdminRestClient implements KeycloakAdminGateway {
    public KeycloakAdminRestClient(RestClient client, KeycloakAdminProperties properties) {}
}

public class KeycloakAdminException extends RuntimeException {}
```

```java
@Bean
KeycloakAdminGateway keycloakAdminGateway(/* your own config binding */) {
    var props = new KeycloakAdminProperties(baseUrl, realm, clientId, clientSecret,
            Duration.ofSeconds(5), Duration.ofSeconds(10));
    return new KeycloakAdminRestClient(RestClient.builder().baseUrl(props.baseUrl()).build(), props);
}
```

**No field has a default, and no secret lives in code.** `KeycloakAdminProperties` rejects a missing or blank `baseUrl`, `realm`, `clientId` or `clientSecret` **at construction**, so an unconfigured environment fails at startup — where failing costs least — instead of running pointed at the wrong realm.

**Every failure leaves as `KeycloakAdminException`**, naming the operation and preserving the cause, and therefore becomes **502** in the `gems-exception` envelope. Letting an HTTP client exception escape would deliver a third party's unavailability to the consumer as a 500.

The technical token is obtained via `client_credentials` and cached in memory until near expiry; a 401 invalidates the cache and the call is retried **exactly once**.

---

### gems-security-authorization

**Package:** `br.com.gems.security.authorization`
**Auto-configuration:** none — the action enum belongs to the consumer
**Activation:** none

Authorization is by **concrete action**, never by generic role.

```java
public interface AuthorizationAction {
    String name();                 // format AREA_VERB — an enum already provides it
    AuthorizationScope scope();
}
public enum AuthorizationScope { GLOBAL, TENANT }

public record AuthorizationCatalog(Set<String> globalActions, Set<String> tenantActions) {
    static <E extends Enum<E> & AuthorizationAction> AuthorizationCatalog of(Class<E> actions);
}
```

The canonical form is `AuthorizationCatalog.of(<enum>)`: a mistyped action does not compile. Actions must match `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*_[A-Z0-9_]+$` (a bare `GESTOR` is rejected), and the global and tenant sets must be disjoint. The canonical constructor stays public for synthetic catalogues in tests and for loading actions from another source — validation is identical on both paths.

**Endpoint intent annotations** — `@PublicEndpoint`, `@GlobalEndpoint`, `@TenantEndpoint`.

```java
public final class EndpointAuthorizationScan {
    record Violation(String endpoint, String reason) {}
    static List<Violation> scan(RequestMappingHandlerMapping mapping, AuthorizationCatalog catalog);
    static List<Violation> scan(Collection<HandlerMethod> methods, AuthorizationCatalog catalog);
    static void assertProtected(RequestMappingHandlerMapping mapping, AuthorizationCatalog catalog);
    static void assertProtected(Collection<HandlerMethod> methods, AuthorizationCatalog catalog);
}
// assertProtected throws UnprotectedEndpointException. Wire it into a test so the build fails
// on an unmarked endpoint — there is no silent default.
```

```java
public interface AuthorizationContextAware { JwtAuthorizationContext authorizationContext(); }
public final class TenantAuthorizationInterceptor implements HandlerInterceptor {}
```

`TenantAuthorizationInterceptor` **fails closed** on a `@TenantEndpoint`: authentication that does not implement `AuthorizationContextAware`, absent authentication, or a context with no alias all refuse. The refusal is `AccessDeniedException`, which `gems-exception` returns as **403** — not 401: whoever got there is authenticated; what is missing is scope, and sending them to login would fix nothing.

**The frontend action list is generated, not maintained:**

```java
public final class FrontendActionCatalogGenerator {
    static <E extends Enum<E> & AuthorizationAction> String generate(Class<E> actions);
    static <E extends Enum<E> & AuthorizationAction> void writeTo(Path target, Class<E> actions);
    static <E extends Enum<E> & AuthorizationAction> void verify(Path target, Class<E> actions);
    // verify throws GeneratedCatalogOutOfDateException
}
// Output: {"global": [...], "tenant": [...]}, sorted, fixed format — so two runs over the same
// enum produce identical files and verify() does not report drift where there is none.
```

Wire `verify` into a test or the build. From then on the frontend list is a **consequence** of the enum, not a third copy kept in parity by hand.

---

### gems-aws

**Package:** `br.com.gems.aws`
**Auto-configuration:** `GemsAwsAutoConfiguration`
**Activation:** `aws.s3.enabled=true`

#### S3Service — injected as Spring bean

```java
// Generate a temporary pre-signed PUT URL for direct client upload
PresignedUrlResponseDTO generatePresignedUploadUrl(GenerateUploadUrlRequestDTO request)

// Generate a temporary pre-signed GET URL for download
PresignedUrlResponseDTO generatePresignedDownloadUrl(String fileKey)

// Delete a file permanently
void deleteFile(String fileKey)

// Check if a file exists (HEAD request — no download)
boolean fileExists(String fileKey)
```

#### DTOs

```java
// Request
GenerateUploadUrlRequestDTO {
    String fileName;       // required
    String contentType;    // required (e.g. "image/jpeg")
    String directory;      // optional — prefix within the bucket
}

// Response (both upload and download)
PresignedUrlResponseDTO {
    String url;     // pre-signed URL
    String fileKey; // full key in the bucket (use for download/delete)
}
```

#### Configuration

```yaml
aws:
  s3:
    enabled: true
    region: us-east-1          # required
    bucket-name: my-bucket     # required
    access-key: ...            # optional; falls back to IAM role
    secret-key: ...            # optional; falls back to IAM role
    endpoint-url: ...          # optional; for LocalStack / MinIO
    presigned-url-expiration-minutes: 15  # default: 15
```

---

### gems-aws-web

**Package:** `br.com.gems.aws.web`
**Auto-configuration:** `GemsAwsWebAutoConfiguration`
**Activation:** `aws.s3.enabled=true` (same flag as gems-aws) + servlet web app required

Registers `S3Controller` at `/api/aws/s3`:

| Method | Path | Body / Param | Response |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/aws/s3/generate-upload-url` | `GenerateUploadUrlRequestDTO` | `PresignedUrlResponseDTO` |
| GET | `/api/aws/s3/generate-download-url` | `?fileKey=...` | `PresignedUrlResponseDTO` |
| DELETE | `/api/aws/s3/delete-file` | `?fileKey=...` | 204 No Content |

Add `gems-aws-web` only if you want these endpoints exposed. Use `gems-aws` alone if you want only the service bean.

---

### gems-rest-common

**Package:** `br.com.gems.rest`
**Auto-configuration:** `GemsRestCommonAutoConfiguration`
**Activation:** `gems.rest.correlation-id.enabled=true` (default: true, servlet apps only)

#### ApiResponseDTO<T>

```java
// Static factories
ApiResponseDTO.ok(T data)
ApiResponseDTO.ok(T data, String message)

// Fields
boolean success;   // always true
String message;
T data;
LocalDateTime timestamp;
```

#### PageResponseDTO<T>

```java
// Static factory
PageResponseDTO.from(Page<T> page)  // converts Spring Page to serializable DTO

// Fields
List<T> content;
int page;
int size;
long totalElements;
int totalPages;
boolean first;
boolean last;
```

#### CorrelationIdFilter (registered automatically)

- Reads `X-Correlation-Id` request header or generates a UUID
- Puts the value in SLF4J MDC under key `correlationId`
- Returns the value in the `X-Correlation-Id` response header
- Clears MDC in `finally`

---

### gems-validation

**Package:** `br.com.gems.validation`
**No auto-configuration needed** — discovered by Jakarta Bean Validation via `@Constraint`.

```java
// Annotations — apply to String fields
@ValidCpf    // message: "CPF inválido"
@ValidCnpj   // message: "CNPJ inválido"
@ValidEmail  // message: "E-mail inválido"
```

All three constraints treat `null` as **valid**. Always combine with `@NotNull` if the field is required:

```java
public class CadastroDTO {
    @NotNull
    @ValidCpf
    private String cpf;

    @NotNull
    @ValidEmail
    private String email;
}
```

---

### gems-openapi

**Package:** `br.com.gems.openapi`
**Auto-configuration:** `GemsOpenApiAutoConfiguration`
**Activation:** `gems.openapi.enabled=true` (default: true)
**Classpath requirement:** `springdoc-openapi-starter-webmvc-ui` must be present

```yaml
gems:
  openapi:
    enabled: true
    title: "Minha API"
    description: "Descrição da API"
    version: "v1"
    contact-name: "Time GEMS"
    contact-email: "gems@exemplo.com"
```

Creates a single `OpenAPI` bean. Consumer can override with their own `@Bean OpenAPI`.

---

### gems-observability

**Package:** `br.com.gems.observability`
**Auto-configuration:** `GemsObservabilityAutoConfiguration`
**Activation:** `gems.observability.enabled=true` (default: true)
**Requirements:** `ObservationRegistry` bean must be present (from `spring-boot-starter-actuator`)

Registers `ObservedAspect`, enabling the `@Observed` annotation on Spring-managed bean methods:

```java
@Observed(name = "usuario.buscar")
public Usuario buscarPorId(UUID id) { ... }
```

---

## Common Patterns

### Exception handling in a service

```java
@Service
@RequiredArgsConstructor
public class UsuarioService {

    public Usuario buscar(UUID id) {
        return usuarioRepository.findById(id)
            .orElseThrow(() -> new BusinessException("Usuário não encontrado"));
    }

    public void validarAcesso(String token) {
        if (!tokenValido(token)) {
            throw new SecurityException("Token inválido ou expirado");
        }
    }
}
```

### REST controller with response envelopes

```java
@RestController
@RequestMapping("/api/usuarios")
@RequiredArgsConstructor
public class UsuarioController {

    private final UsuarioService usuarioService;

    @GetMapping("/{id}")
    public ResponseEntity<ApiResponseDTO<UsuarioDTO>> buscar(@PathVariable UUID id) {
        UsuarioDTO dto = usuarioService.buscar(id);
        return ResponseEntity.ok(ApiResponseDTO.ok(dto));
    }

    @GetMapping
    public ResponseEntity<PageResponseDTO<UsuarioDTO>> listar(Pageable pageable) {
        Page<UsuarioDTO> page = usuarioService.listar(pageable);
        return ResponseEntity.ok(PageResponseDTO.from(page));
    }
}
```

### S3 upload flow

```java
@Service
@RequiredArgsConstructor
public class DocumentoService {

    private final S3Service s3Service;

    public PresignedUrlResponseDTO gerarUrlUpload(String fileName, String contentType) {
        var request = GenerateUploadUrlRequestDTO.builder()
            .fileName(fileName)
            .contentType(contentType)
            .directory("documentos/")
            .build();
        return s3Service.generatePresignedUploadUrl(request);
    }
}
```

### ModelMapper strict mapping

```java
@Service
@RequiredArgsConstructor
public class UsuarioService {

    public UsuarioDTO toDTO(Usuario entity) {
        return ModelMapperUtils.mapStrict(entity, UsuarioDTO.class);
    }
}
```

### Custom HQL repository

```java
@Repository
public interface UsuarioRepository extends JpaRepository<Usuario, UUID>,
                                           BaseCustomJpaRepository<Usuario> {

    default Page<UsuarioDTO> buscarAtivos(Pageable pageable) {
        var hql = new StringBuilder("SELECT u FROM Usuario u WHERE u.ativo = true");
        return this.executeHql(hql, pageable, UsuarioDTO.class);
    }
}

@Service
@RequiredArgsConstructor
public class UsuarioService {

    private final UsuarioRepository usuarioRepository;

    public Page<UsuarioDTO> buscarAtivos(Pageable pageable) {
        return usuarioRepository.buscarAtivos( pageable );
    }
}
```

---

## Property Reference (all activation flags)

```yaml
# gems-jpa (default: false — prevents conflict with app's @EnableJpaRepositories)
gems:
  jpa:
    enabled: true
    base-packages: br.com.seuprojeto   # package to scan for JPA entities/repos

# gems-jpa-multi-tenant (default: false)
  tenant:
    enabled: true
    schema-prefix: tenant_          # default since 3.0.0; read ONLY by TenantSchemaNaming
    global-schema: administracao    # no default; TenantScope.global() fails without it
    client-query: SELECT DS_SIGLA_CLIENT FROM tenant_configuration.client
    liquibase:
      changelog: db/changelog/changelog-multi-schemas.xml

# gems-auditing (default: false)
  auditing:
    enabled: true
    schema: auditoria               # MANDATORY, no default — the app will not start without it

# gems-mapstruct, gems-keycloak-admin, gems-security-authorization: no properties,
# no auto-configuration. The consumer declares the beans.

# gems-aws / gems-aws-web (default: false)
aws:
  s3:
    enabled: true
    region: us-east-1
    bucket-name: meu-bucket
    access-key: AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE     # optional
    secret-key: wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG   # optional
    endpoint-url: http://localhost:4566  # optional (LocalStack/MinIO)
    presigned-url-expiration-minutes: 15 # optional, default: 15

# gems-rest-common (default: true)
gems:
  rest:
    correlation-id:
      enabled: true

# gems-openapi (default: true)
  openapi:
    enabled: true
    title: "Minha API"
    description: "Descrição da API"
    version: "v1"
    contact-name: "Time GEMS"
    contact-email: "contato@exemplo.com"

# gems-observability (default: true)
  observability:
    enabled: true
```
